response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration > 5 GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS bench FROM per_rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day, p.films, p.avg_rate_per_day / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages computed over the filtered films (rental_duration > 5), so 'all ratings' means the rating groups that survive the filter.
Films with rental_duration > 5 means durations of 6 or 7 days; the filter is applied before grouping.
CAST to DOUBLE avoids MySQL's DECIMAL division truncation, so the averages are unrounded as requested.
rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL, so AVG ignores no rows in practice; the benchmark is NULL only when no rating groups remain, in which case zero rows are returned.

alternatives.interpretation: The benchmark uses per-rating averages computed over all films regardless of rental_duration, while the reported per-rating averages and counts still use only films with rental_duration > 5.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration > 5 GROUP BY rating), all_ratings AS (SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / rental_duration) AS avg_all FROM film GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_all) AS bench FROM all_ratings) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day, p.films, p.avg_rate_per_day / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL;
